notes: Site: IKEA UK (ikea.com/gb/en). Tier 1 (curl HTTP fetch) of the homepage confirmed only the mega-menu nav JSON was present in raw HTML (no product grid data - client-rendered), so escalated to tier 2 (Playwright/Chromium) per access tier order. Found the site's own main nav 'hot' links exposing 'Best sellers' -> https://www.ikea.com/gb/en/cat/best-sellers/ repeated for multiple category contexts (e.g. Lighting, Furniture, Kitchenware) all pointing to the SAME base URL with only a '?filters=f-subcategories:<catID>' query param difference - these are facet filters on one underlying listing, not separate site-curated PLPs, so only the canonical unfiltered URL is emitted (no invented sub-categories). Opened https://www.ikea.com/gb/en/cat/best-sellers/ with Playwright: page heading 'Best sellers', on-page copy 'Ever wondered what our top selling items are? From timeless furniture classics to this year's most popular products, you can find our best sellers here.' - a genuine bestseller/popularity merchandising concept, real product grid with sort/filter, not editorial. Header shows '303 items' (appears twice - page header + filter panel) and the results-list footer independently confirms 'Showing 24 of 303 results', so the two numbers cross-check exactly - qty verified reliable. No other Bestsellers-labelled entry point found in nav, footer, or the New/Offers hubs. Did not need Claude-in-Chrome (tier 3).
